# Inventory file reference

An inventory file lists the devices port49 serves: their names, platforms, addresses, attributes and the key
that admits each. It is one YAML document; an unknown key (a typo such as `keyref:` for `key_ref:`) or a second
document is refused, so a mistake cannot silently un-pin a device onto a group key.

The `key_groups:` block is read from the policy file, where key assignment is reviewed. A block here still
loads, with a notice, until it is moved; where both files have one, the policy file's wins.

Paths below use `[]` for an item of a list.

## `devices`

| Key | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `devices.[].name` | string | The device's name, which policy scopes, tests and the log use. |
| `devices.[].platform` | string | The device's platform, lowercase letters, digits and `_`, matching an adapter in the pinned platform set or one the policy file defines. A platform with no adapter gets the generic one. |
| `devices.[].addresses` | list of string | The IP addresses the device's connections come from, as a list. A connection is matched to its device by source address. |
| `devices.[].attributes` | map of string | Free key and value pairs, such as `site`, `role` and `os_version`, that scopes match on and key groups can match on. |
| `devices.[].key_ref` | string | Pins the device to one key, by name. The key is a name that the policy file's `keys:` block (or port49d's) defines; it never holds the secret. |
| `devices.[].transport` | string | How the device speaks TACACS+: `tcp` (default), obfuscated under a shared key, or `tls`, mutual TLS with no shared key. Any other value makes the device refused rather than the file. |

## `key_groups`

| Key | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `key_groups.[].match.cidr` | string | Matches the devices whose address is in this prefix, written without host bits. A group needs `cidr` or `attributes`; one with neither is refused. |
| `key_groups.[].match.attributes` | map of string | Matches the devices whose attributes equal all of these pairs. |
| `key_groups.[].key_ref` | string | The key that devices in the group are admitted under. Required. A key name: lowercase letters, digits and `_`, starting with a letter, at most 64, and not the reserved `single_device`. |
